operator_io_quirks: Backtick-quoted identifiers in DDL; column `len` is a SQL keyword-ish name (also `position`, `shape`) — must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
Column named `len` (TEXT) — name collides with SQL length function; quoting required.
DDL has `len`TEXT` (no space between backtick and type) — line-based unique/check scan and type parse must tolerate.
FK cars.train_id -> trains.id, parent exists, parent PK unique; ON DELETE/UPDATE CASCADE declared.
Table order: trains (level 0) before cars (level 1); cars depends on trains.
Tiny tables (63 and 20 rows) — original_values fully read, no sampling needed.
All columns null_rate 0.0 in original, but all non-PK columns are DEFAULT NULL / notnull=0 — TS may still emit NULLs via FK-empty-parent path.
No unique/check constraints beyond PKs; no composite keys; no self-FK.
Storage classes match declared types everywhere (integer/text) — no contradictions.
distinct counts tiny (2-5) for most cars columns — literal pool will be small; String sampler length range narrow.
trains.id distinct=20 = row count; cars.train_id distinct=20 = parent size (all parents referenced).
cars.id distinct=63 = row count; position distinct=4, load_num distinct=4 (small domains).
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer for all INTEGER columns (id, train_id, position, wheels, load_num): uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale from type args (none -> default), then +-1/+-2 perturbation; produces implausible ids/positions.

String fuzzer for TEXT columns (shape, len, sides, roof, load_shape, direction): random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() length 0..20, plus 50% contaminate; will not reproduce enum-like values (rectangle, east, short) unless in literal pool.
PK columns (cars.id, trains.id) get max_l0=inf -> always fresh Number draws; PK dedup keeps first occurrence, so many rows dropped for small target sizes.
FK cars.train_id drawn from trains.id final values with replacement -> duplicates in child, fine; if trains empty -> NULLs.

Expected FN drivers: Number fuzzer emits ids/positions outside the tiny real domains (position 1-4, wheels 2-3, load_num 0-3) so predicates like position=2 or wheels=3 rarely match; String fuzzer rarely hits 'east'/'west'/'short'/'long' enums.

Expected FP drivers: no ties/duplicates in original (all distinct counts = row counts for ids), but TS injects duplicate train_id/position/load_num values -> queries with DISTINCT/COUNT/GROUP BY may agree spuriously; also empty-parent NULL train_id can make joins drop rows consistently.
String contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop char) makes shape/roof values near-misses of real enums -> LIKE '%east%' style predicates may flip.
Small tables: choose_table_sizes may produce sizes far from 63/20 (up to 2500 or 30+200u) -> cardinality-sensitive queries (COUNT) diverge from original but that is expected TS behaviour.
No Date/Time/Bool columns -> those fuzzers unused here.
Literal pool from train SQL will seed shape/roof/direction enums if present in gold/candidate SQL; otherwise String fuzzer dominates.
